result.title: Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation
result.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) supervises student-generated responses using sampled-token student-teacher log-ratios. A positive log-ratio penalizes a token that the student assigns higher probability to than the teacher, but its current value does not distinguish sustained high penalties from abrupt increases along a response. We examine these local changes by comparing consecutive blocks of tokens within the same response. Our diagnostic identifies penalty jumps, abrupt increases in average penalty that persist on held-out tokens. Across these jumps, penalties rise while teacher confidence decreases. We call this pattern penalty-confidence tension. Boundaries into high-penalty blocks do not exhibit comparable confidence changes, showing that local changes provide information beyond the current penalty value. Motivated by this observation, we propose Adaptive Pullback OPD (AP-OPD). At each detected jump, AP-OPD uses the preceding block as a local reference and uniformly scales all supervision coefficients in the following block so that its weighted average penalty matches the preceding block's original mean. This reference determines the scaling factor without an additional strength constant. AP-OPD improves performance on both mathematical reasoning and code generation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断 on-policy 蒸馏中同一回复内学生-教师 log-ratio 的局部突变，发现「惩罚跳变」处惩罚上升而教师置信度下降，据此提出 AP-OPD：在检测到跳变时以前一块为局部参照，统一缩放后续块的监督系数，使加权平均惩罚对齐前一块原均值，并在数学推理与代码生成上报告提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作不含视觉或 latent 状态，但按块检测监督信号突变并自适应缩放系数、且免设强度常数的做法，可能可供核查 LVR 轨迹训练中的步级贡献分配与监督强度标定。
